effects: Pulls exactly `assets` USDC (vault asset 0xb883…630f) from the signer into the vault (enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
Mints feUSDCv2 shares to `onBehalf`. The amount is previewDeposit(assets), set by the current share price after accrueInterest. The caller cannot set a minimum.
Accrues interest and may mint fee shares to the fee recipients first. This dilutes the price used for the signer's shares.
Sends the deposited USDC on to the liquidity adapter. This does not change the signer's position.
formats.shown: Deposit 40 USDC for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker feUSDCv2 and the share recipient shown. The number of shares received is not shown.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted is not shown, because it is computed from the vault's share price
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. There is no minShares parameter. Case 0: 40e18 feUSDCv2 minted to the signer, and the screen only shows 'Share ticker: feUSDCv2'.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds the amount. A label such as 'Receive feUSDCv2 shares (amount set by vault price)' would at least say that shares arrive.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' field is a static constant, so it reads like a value but carries no amount
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'}. Case 0 screen: 'Share ticker: feUSDCv2'.
findings.fix: Relabel it, for example 'You receive: feUSDCv2 vault shares'.

cases.notes: The 40 USDC leaving is shown exactly. The 40 feUSDCv2 arriving is shown by asset and recipient only, without the amount. The amount is derived from storage.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns feUSDCv2 shares from `onBehalf`. The amount is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up and set by the share price. The caller cannot set a maximum.
Sends exactly `assets` USDC from the vault to `receiver`.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, spends the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` by the number of shares burned.
Accrues interest and fee shares first. This may pull liquidity from the liquidity adapter.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 1 USDC to <receiver>, with the Owner shown. The number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of shares burned from the owner is not shown, because it is computed from the share price
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`, and exit runs `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 2: 1e18 feUSDCv2 burned from the signer, and no share field is on the screen.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds it. The Owner label could read 'Burn feUSDCv2 shares from' so the share outflow is stated.

cases.notes: The 1 USDC arriving is shown exactly with its recipient. The 1 feUSDCv2 burned is not stated. The reader guessed only that the position drops.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Sends USDC to `receiver`. The amount is previewRedeem(shares), rounded down and set by the share price. There is no minimum received.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, spends the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` by `shares`.
Accrues interest and fee shares first. This may pull liquidity from the liquidity adapter.
formats.shown: Redeem 40 feUSDCv2 to <receiver>, with the Owner shown. Nothing names the asset received (USDC) or its amount.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names USDC as the asset paid out, though the descriptor has the constant
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets)`. The redeem fields are only shares, receiver and onBehalf. mint uses `$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker`, but redeem does not. Case 3: 40 USDC in to the signer, and the screen does not mention USDC.
findings.fix: Add a field {label:'Receive asset', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'}, or name USDC in the intent, for example 'Redeem {shares} for USDC to {receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received has no bound in the calldata, so the screen cannot show it
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. There is no minAssets parameter. Case 3: 40e6 USDC received, and no amount is shown.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. A label could say the amount is set by the vault share price.

cases.notes: The 40 feUSDCv2 out is shown exactly. The USDC in is not on the screen. The reader guessed USDC from the share name and could not know the amount.

effects: Pulls USDC from the signer. The amount is previewMint(shares), rounded up and set by the share price. There is no maximum the signer can set.
Accrues interest and fee shares first, then sends the USDC on to the liquidity adapter.
formats.shown: Mint 1 feUSDCv2 for <onBehalf>. The deposit asset is shown as 'USDC' with no amount.

findings.title: mint: the USDC amount taken from the signer is not shown, because the share price computes it
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`, and enter runs `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: 1e6 USDC out from the signer, and the screen shows only 'Deposit asset: USDC'.
findings.fix: No calldata field holds it. The label could read 'Pays USDC (amount set by vault price)'.

findings.title: mint: the intent says 'Mint' and the sentence never says USDC leaves the signer's wallet
findings.evidence: descriptor mint: intent 'Mint', interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. Case 1: 'Mint 1 feUSDCv2 for 0x…dEaD', while 1 USDC left the signer.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit USDC' and interpolatedIntent 'Pay USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The shares went to 0x…dEaD (signer null), and that recipient is shown correctly. The signer's only effect, 1 USDC out, is shown as an asset with no amount.
